findings.title: drain_mailbox_parallel deadline (120s) is shorter than its own loop deadline (180s)
findings.body: `drain_mailbox_parallel` loops until `deadline = timezone.now() + BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET` (line 294). `BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET` is `timedelta(minutes=BACKOFF_INTERVAL)` and `BACKOFF_INTERVAL = 3` (`src/sentry/hybridcloud/models/webhookpayload.py:18`), so the loop is designed to run for up to 180s and only checks the deadline between batches (line 301). The new `processing_deadline_duration=120` is lower than that. With a deep backlog, which is the case the loop exists for, the taskworker will hit the 120s processing deadline mid-loop and fail or retry the task before it ends normally. The 180s cap is then never reached, and the in-flight batch is cut off. `drain_mailbox` (300s) leaves room for 180s plus one delivery, so the two are inconsistent. Set the parallel deadline to at least the 180s loop budget plus one batch of delivery timeouts, e.g. 300 like `drain_mailbox`.

findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay event timestamps (likely milliseconds)
findings.body: `gen_request_data` interleaves errors and recording events with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error timestamp is the nodestore event `timestamp`, a float in epoch seconds (line 115). The recording event's top-level `timestamp` is an rrweb timestamp. As far as I know rrweb timestamps are epoch milliseconds, but I did not find a conversion in `event_parser.py`. If so, every error compares as earlier than the first event. All errors are then emitted before the first breadcrumb, and the chronological ordering this PR claims is lost. The tests mask this: they use seconds for both (`tests/sentry/replays/test_project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:149,188`) and have one event. Normalize the units before comparing, e.g. convert the error timestamp to ms, and add a test with realistic ms event timestamps and several events.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs ids with results by position
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id. Its order is not the input order: items fetched from the service come first, then `items.update(cache_items)` appends cached ones (`src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:198-206`). It also deduplicates the ids, and missing ids are omitted. Zipping `error_ids` against `events.values()` can therefore attach the wrong event id to the wrong data. The `id` isn't used in the log text today, but the `ErrorEvent.id` is wrong. Build `node_id -> event_id` and iterate over `events.items()` instead.

findings.title: Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled
findings.body: `query_replay_instance` and `process_raw_response` run (lines 70-84) before the `enable_error_context=false` check at line 87. When the caller disables error context, the ClickHouse query result is thrown away. Move the query into the `else` branch.

findings.title: Dead _handle_regex_match left in parametrize_w_experiments
findings.body: After removing the `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` branch, the local `_handle_regex_match` closure (lines 335-343) is no longer called. The only call was in the deleted `else` branch. Remove it.

findings.title: age/timestamp exclusivity validators don't enforce what their docstrings say
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` only run when their own field is present. A report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` therefore validates, although the docstrings say one must be present. Both are `required=False`, so nothing else enforces it. The checks use truthiness (`initial_data.get("age")`), so `age: 0` together with a `timestamp` passes both validators. The docstring on `validate_timestamp` ("age is absent, but timestamp is present") also reads backwards. Use a `validate()` method that checks `("age" in data) != ("timestamp" in data)`.

findings.title: Changing the autofix tuning default silently turns off automation for existing projects
findings.body: `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` is read with `project.get_option(...)` in `_is_issue_fixable` (`src/sentry/seer/issue_summary.py:253`), and `off` returns False. Projects that never set the option currently resolve to `low`, so the registry default change from `low` to `off` stops automation for all of them without a migration or notice. The same applies to the org default in `constants.py:724`. Is this intended for existing projects, or only for newly created ones? If only for new ones, the default should be applied at project creation (see `set_default_project_autofix_automation_tuning`) rather than by changing the global default.

findings.title: Analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` check at line 88. Calls from orgs without the feature, which get a 404, are counted as assemble requests. If the event should measure actual usage, record it after the gate.

findings.title: Flag branch renders an always-empty table
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is on, `TableWidgetVisualization` receives `columns={[]}` and empty `data`, so every table widget renders empty and ignores `result.data` and `result.meta`. The flag is not registered anywhere in the repository (the only match is this line), so it can't be enabled yet. If the flag is later registered before the wiring lands, tables go blank. Either wire the real `columns` and `tableData` from `result`, or leave this branch out until then.

findings.title: get_environment_info fetches the recommended event for every issue on each merged-PR comment
findings.body: `issue.get_recommended_event()` runs once per issue in the comment's list comprehension, in both the GitHub and GitLab workflows. Each call reads event data from Snuba and nodestore, serially, on the comment task. A slow call blocks the rest, and the broad `except Exception` only handles errors, not latency. Consider fetching the environments in one query for all issues, or bounding the work.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only applied when a search query is typed
findings.body: `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` at line 61-63 when `searchQuery` is empty, so the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check at line 67 never runs in the default view. `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are therefore shown whenever the search box is empty, and they only disappear once the user types something. Apply the hidden-attribute filter before the empty-query early return, e.g. `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name));`.

findings.title: Placeholder's right-hand group lost `align-items: center` and `gap`
findings.body: The removed `FlexBox` styled component set `display:flex; align-items:center; gap: space(1)`. The first replacement group (line 22) keeps `align="center" gap={space(1)}`, but the second group at line 27 is a bare `<Flex>`, so its three 100px placeholders now render with no gap and no vertical centering. The loading skeleton changes visibly. Use `<Flex align="center" gap={space(1)}>` for it too.

findings.title: Query key no longer includes the organization
findings.body: The old key was `[path, endpointOptions]`, and the path contained `organization.slug`. The new key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `queryOptions` (built by `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` in useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:29-53) has itemType, attributeType, project, substringMatch and the datetime fields, but no organization. Two organizations with the same page filters (e.g. no project selected, same period) share a cache entry, and the shared react-query cache can serve the other org's attribute keys until the refetch finishes. Add `organization.slug` to the key.

findings.title: Switching to raw `useQuery` drops `retry: false` and changes what `isLoading` means
findings.body: The previous `useApiQuery` call set `retry: false`, `staleTime: 0` and `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. The raw `useQuery` uses the client defaults (DEFAULT_QUERY_CLIENT_CONFIG in utils/queryClient.tsx:19-26 only turns off refetch on reconnect and on window focus), so retry is react-query's default of 3 with backoff. When `/trace-items/attributes/` fails, `isLoading` (now `isFetching`, line 61) stays true through the retries, so `TraceItemAttributeProvider` (contexts/traceItemAttributeContext.tsx:43-57) reports string and number attributes as loading for several seconds. It also reports loading on every background refetch, not just the first load without data. `attributes` can now be `undefined`; the provider's spreads tolerate that, but the return type changed. Consider `retry: false` and `isLoading` from the query result if the old behaviour was intended.

findings.title: `height: 100%` dropped from the replaced FlexBox
findings.body: The removed `FlexBox` had `flex-grow: 1; flex-direction: column; height: 100%`. `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` sets `flex: 1 1 0%` and no height. If the parent is not a flex container, or relies on the child's `height: 100%`, the waterfall's height can change. Please confirm against the parent layout in the trace view.

findings.title: TestGetCommentBody expects environment names but is not a Snuba test case
findings.body: `test_simple` now expects ` in `dev`` / ` in `prod``. That text comes from `CommitContextIntegration.get_environment_info` (src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:584-597). It calls `issue.get_recommended_event()`, which queries Snuba (src/sentry/models/group.py:274, 870). `TestGetCommentBody` inherits only `GithubCommentTestCase` (an `IntegrationTestCase`), not `SnubaTestCase`. Only `SnubaTestCase.store_event` (src/sentry/testutils/cases.py:1058-1068) routes events into Snuba, so these events are probably never there. The lookup would return no event, or fail inside the swallowed `except Exception`, and the comment would have no ` in ...` suffix, so the assertion would fail. Make the class also inherit `SnubaTestCase`, as `TestTop5IssuesByCount` does a few lines above, or mock `get_environment_info`.

findings.title: GitLab TestGetCommentBody has the same missing Snuba dependency for the environment suffix
findings.body: The expected comment includes ` in `dev`` and ` in `prod``. These come from `get_environment_info`, which queries Snuba through `Group.get_recommended_event`. `TestGetCommentBody(GitlabCommentTestCase)` is not a `SnubaTestCase`, so `store_event` does not write to Snuba and the environment lookup most likely returns an empty string. Add `SnubaTestCase` to the class bases, or mock the lookup.

findings.title: No test posts with `application/reports+json` any more
findings.body: The old tests posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"`, the media type browsers send and the one `BrowserReportsJSONParser` handles (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:63-69, 82). The rewritten tests (`test_basic`, `test_handles_multiple_reports_both_specs`, and every validation test) all use the client's default format. The only test that sets a content type is the 415 one, which uses `bad/type/json`. Nothing now checks that the custom parser accepts the real content type. Pass `content_type="application/reports+json"` in at least `test_basic`. The assertion on the `browser_report_received` log call was also dropped, although the endpoint still logs it (line 93).

findings.title: `Flex.Item grow={1}` is not equivalent to the removed `flex: 1`
findings.body: The removed `FlexContainer` used `flex: 1`, which is `1 1 0%`. `Flex.Item grow={1}` renders `flex-grow:1; flex-shrink:1; flex-basis:auto` (static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:35-46). With an auto basis, a long description or feature list gets a larger starting size, and the sibling `Metadata` block (line 362, a fixed-margin grid) shrinks in proportion. The previous layout kept `Metadata` at its natural width. `<Flex.Item flex="1">` reproduces the old behaviour exactly.

findings.title: `division by zero` assertion can't tell title from message
findings.body: The endpoint builds the log line as `'{title}: {message}'` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:126-131). `title` and `message` come from different nodestore keys (lines 114 and 116). For a ZeroDivisionError the stored title is normally already `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero`. So `assert any("division by zero" in log ...)` passes even if `message` comes back empty, and the test would not catch a bad `message` lookup. Assert the exact expected line instead, or build the event so `title` and `message` hold different strings. The test also never checks where the error line falls among the breadcrumbs. The ordering is only covered by the unit test at line 283.

findings.title: No PUT test for omitting `owner` while one is already set
findings.body: `update()` in src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:66-79 has three branches: set the owner, clear it when `owner` is None, and do nothing when the key is absent (`"owner" in validated_data`). The new tests cover the first two. The third is not covered: every pre-existing PUT test sends `valid_data` without `owner` on a detector that has none. A regression that wipes the owner on any PUT without `owner` would pass the suite. Add a test that sets an owner, sends `valid_data` without `owner`, and asserts the owner is unchanged. The PUT path also has no test for an invalid owner or one from another organization. Only the POST tests (test_organization_detector_index.py:511-542) cover those.

contracts.before_after: The loop stops itself at now+BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET (3 min), checked only between batches (lines 294-312). The new task deadline of 120s is below that, so the task can be killed before its own deadline.
contracts.visible_effect: With a deep backlog, webhook delivery tasks are killed or retried at 120s mid-batch instead of ending cleanly at 180s.
contracts.failure_mode: An in-flight batch is cut off by the taskworker. The batch may be re-delivered or leave the records' attempt state inconsistent.

contracts.action: Error context fetched from nodestore and interleaved into the replay summary request
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous get_request_data over recording segments only
contracts.before_after: Before, only recording-event log lines were sent to Seer. Now error log lines are merged by comparing the error's seconds timestamp with the event's top-level timestamp. Failures in fetch_error_details are swallowed with capture_exception and return an empty list.
contracts.visible_effect: The Seer summary receives error lines. Their order depends on the timestamp units matching.
contracts.failure_mode: A nodestore failure silently yields a summary without errors. A unit mismatch puts all errors first.
contracts.open_question: Are top-level timestamps in stored replay recording segments in milliseconds? I did not find a conversion in the parser or any ms/seconds handling.

contracts.action: Workflow engine delayed processing now fetches slow conditions once and passes them down
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous per-function get_slow_conditions_for_groups calls using event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys() and event_data.dcg_ids
contracts.before_after: Both previous calls covered the same id set as event_data.dcg_ids (dcg_to_groups is built from the same key.dcg_ids). The single call at line 652 produces a dict covering every id in dcg_ids, so the later dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] lookups cannot KeyError.
contracts.visible_effect: No behavior change beyond one fewer fetch and a new info log.

contracts.equivalent_path: Other owner ActorField usages in serializers
contracts.before_after: ActorField.to_internal_value reads self.context["organization"]. The create and update paths already use context["organization"] elsewhere in this validator. The owner is saved by instance.save() on update and by Detector.objects.create on create.
contracts.visible_effect: The API can set or clear the detector owner.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing organization in the context would raise KeyError, but update and create already rely on it.

contracts.action: TableWidgetVisualization renders a GridEditable from TabularData, with default head/body cell renderers that fall back from custom renderers
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing dashboard table widget rendering through GridEditable plus getFieldRenderer in utils/discover/fieldRenderers
contracts.before_after: New component. Before rendering it derives columns from `columns` or from `tableData.meta.fields`. Each cell calls the custom renderer first, then falls back to `getFieldRenderer(columnKey, meta.fields, false)` with organization, location, unit and theme.
contracts.visible_effect: Table of headers and typed cell values; empty `data` renders GridEditable's empty state; `LoadingPlaceholder` renders GridEditable with `isLoading`.
contracts.failure_mode: No async call. A `columns` entry whose key is missing from `meta.fields` falls through getFieldRenderer's default renderer, so it does not throw. `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields)` would throw only if `tableData` were undefined, but it is a required prop.

contracts.action: Visualize now holds a single yAxis; AggregateColumnEditorModal applies columns as JSON; Visualize.fromJSON returns an array
contracts.equivalent_path: toolbarVisualize's setVisualizes path, which already calls toJSON() before writing to the URL
contracts.before_after: Before, the modal passed `Visualize` instances to `onColumnsChange`, and `updateLocationWithAggregateFields` ran `isBaseVisualize` on them. Now it maps `isVisualize(col) ? col.toJSON() : col`, so `isBaseVisualize` matches and `fromJSON(...)` expands each `yAxes` entry into its own serialized visualize. The new `isVisualize` checks `yAxis`. findAllFieldRefs now filters writable params with `isBaseVisualize`, which fixes a latent mismatch.
contracts.visible_effect: Editing aggregate columns writes one `aggregateField` URL entry per y-axis. Saved or URL queries with multiple yAxes in one visualize become separate charts, as getVisualizesFromLocation already did.
contracts.failure_mode: The only caller of `onColumnsChange` for aggregates is tables/index.tsx:81 via `useSetExploreAggregateFields`, which takes BaseAggregateField[]. No failure path found.

contracts.action: useTraceItemAttributeKeys now fetches through useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys using raw useQuery
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous useApiQuery call with retry false, staleTime 0 and no window-focus refetch; the sibling callback hook useGetTraceItemAttributeValues
contracts.before_after: Before: useApiQuery with the org slug in the path and `environment` in the query. After: a shared `queryFn` calls `api.requestPromise` and throws a wrapped Error on failure. `environment` is no longer sent, with a code comment saying it is unsupported. The query key has no org slug, and retry now follows the client default.
contracts.visible_effect: Attribute keys feed TraceItemAttributeProvider and then the search builders and column editors.
contracts.failure_mode: On rejection the hook returns `error`, but the provider ignores it, so attributes stay undefined (static tags only) with no visible error. Retries delay `isLoading` becoming false. The cache key is shared across organizations.

contracts.action: AI summary tab now resolves the project from replayRecord.project_id instead of the `project` URL query param, and shows an error Alert when the project is not found
contracts.equivalent_path: Other replay views that call useProjectFromId with the record's project_id
contracts.before_after: Before: project_id came from the URL query, so a missing `project` param left the query disabled and the tab spinning forever. After: project_id comes from the loaded record, and a project missing from the store gets an explicit error Alert (lines 90-96). While the record is still undefined, project_id is undefined and the loading branch is shown.
contracts.visible_effect: The tab now loads for replays opened without ?project=. A project absent from ProjectsStore shows 'Project not found' instead of an endless spinner.
contracts.failure_mode: No new async call. The query stays disabled when the project is missing, and the Alert covers that case.

contracts.action: PR comment bodies now use the single-issue template with an environment suffix; tests were updated to match
contracts.equivalent_path: CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and get_environment_info, called from the GitHub and GitLab get_comment_body
contracts.before_after: The template is '* ‼️ [**title**](url){env}\n', joined with '\n' and followed by the body template. The expected strings, including the blank-line counts before <sub> on GitHub and the trailing newline on GitLab, match the code. The environment suffix needs a Snuba lookup that the test class does not set up (see findings).
contracts.visible_effect: PR comment text on GitHub and GitLab
contracts.failure_mode: get_environment_info swallows all exceptions and returns an empty string, so a failed lookup silently drops the suffix and the test expectation would then fail

contracts.action: Replay summarize endpoint now looks up the replay's error events and merges them into the breadcrumb log sent to Seer. `enable_error_context=false` skips the lookup.
contracts.before_after: Before: only breadcrumbs went to Seer. After: error ids come from query_replay_instance (lines 70-84), details from nodestore (lines 104-123), and `gen_request_data` merges them by timestamp (lines 142-168). The tests cover the enabled case, the disabled case, and the merge order in a unit test.
contracts.visible_effect: The Seer summary request includes `User experienced an error: ...` lines, and the endpoint responds with Seer's JSON.
contracts.failure_mode: Any exception in `fetch_error_details` is captured and returns `[]` (lines 121-123), so the summary silently omits errors. No test exercises that path.

contracts.action: Detector create and update now accept an `owner` actor identifier, and the tests assert the stored owner and the serialized response.
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:62-79 (update) and 120-138 (create); ActorField in src/sentry/api/fields/actor.py:11-19 validates through parse_and_validate_actor
contracts.before_after: `ActorField` parses the identifier and checks that the user or team belongs to the organization (src/sentry/types/actor.py:275-302). `update` sets the user or team id and clears the other, and clears both on None. `create` does the same. The tests send JSON (the `get_response` default format is json), so `owner: None` is delivered.
contracts.visible_effect: The API response carries `owner` as `user:<id>` or `team:<id>`.
contracts.failure_mode: An invalid or foreign identifier gives a 400 with an `owner` key. Only the POST path tests this.

contracts.action: The new ourlogs top-events test runs `/events-stats/` with `dataset=ourlogs` and `topEvents=5`.
contracts.before_after: The endpoint sends ourlogs through the same RPC top-events path as spans_rpc. The test's expected counts (60, 50, 40, 30, 20 for the top five and 10 for Other) match the fixture sizes. The `message` field resolves to `sentry.body`.
contracts.visible_effect: The response is keyed by message body, with `order` 0 to 4 and an `Other` bucket at order 5.
contracts.failure_mode: No failure path is covered. The test only runs the success case.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 4.** I found one fix-level bug in this part. The `drain_mailbox_parallel` deadline of 120s is shorter than its own 180s loop budget, so the task can be killed mid-batch under backlog. There is one probable bug, medium confidence: the replay summary compares error timestamps in seconds with replay event timestamps that are probably milliseconds, so error ordering may be wrong. I also left several consider-level notes. The main ones are an id/data mispairing in `fetch_error_details`, a Snuba query that runs even when error context is disabled, and the autofix default changing to `off` for existing projects. The rest are smaller: browser-report validators that accept neither `age` nor `timestamp`, and dead code in `parameterization.py`. Nothing was run, and no tests were read except to check what the replay test uses for timestamp units.

**Batch 2 of 4.** I reviewed all 32 files in this part and found two bugs and three lower-confidence concerns. The Visualize single-yAxis refactor looks consistent. `aggregateColumnEditorModal` now calls `toJSON()`, `findAllFieldRefs` filters with `isBaseVisualize`, and I found no leftover `.yAxes` reads on `Visualize` instances. I read the code only and ran no tests.\n\n- **Bug (fix):** the `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter in `eapSections/attributes.tsx` is skipped when the search box is empty, so `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` still show by default.\n- **Bug (fix):** the loading placeholder in `traceTabsAndVitals.tsx` lost `align-items` and `gap` on its second group.\n- **Concern (consider):** the new `useTraceItemAttributeKeys` query key has no organization slug.\n- **Concern (consider):** the same hook now uses react-query's default retry and treats every refetch as loading.\n- **Concern (consider, low confidence):** `traceWaterfall.tsx` dropped `height: 100%` when it moved to `Flex`.

**Batch 3 of 4.** I reviewed the 25 files in this part. Most of it is consistent with the code it tests or replaces: the Flex swaps, the single-yAxis `Visualize` specs, the table widget spec, the removed regex-experiment tests, the 0917 no-op migration test removal, and the "off" autofix default.

- **Fix, likely failing tests:** The GitHub and GitLab `TestGetCommentBody` tests now expect ` in `dev`` and ` in `prod``, but those classes are not `SnubaTestCase`. The environment lookup goes through Snuba and swallows errors, so I expect the suffix to be missing and the assertions to fail. I did not run anything; this rests on reading the test bases and `get_environment_info`.
- **Consider, lost coverage:** No browser-reporting test posts with `application/reports+json` any more, so the custom parser is untested for the media type browsers actually send.
- **Consider, layout:** `Flex.Item grow={1}` is not the same as the old `flex: 1` in `integrationLayout.tsx`. The auto basis could change how the metadata column shrinks.
- **Not checked:** I found no spec for the AI summary tab, and the new "Project not found" alert has no test.

**Batch 4 of 4.** This part is five test files. I found nothing wrong that needs fixing, only two minor test gaps. The replay test for error context asserts `division by zero` in a way that also passes when the error `message` field is empty, because the title already contains it. The detector PUT tests don't check that an existing owner is kept when `owner` is omitted. The workflow_engine delayed-workflow tests correctly pass the new `dcg_to_slow_conditions` argument. The ourlogs top-events test matches the rpc top-events path in the endpoint, and its expected counts (60, 50, 40, 30, 20, with 10 in Other) agree with the fixture. I did not run any tests.
